key_insight: Influenza vaccine effectiveness estimates were similar when calculated from prospective test-negative enrollment and from electronic health record (EHR) data in the 2024–2025 U.S. season.
clinical_relevance: This suggests EHR-based surveillance can provide a practical alternative for monitoring seasonal influenza vaccine effectiveness, while still requiring attention to subgroup differences.
method: Compared vaccine effectiveness using two data sources: prospective test-negative outpatient enrollment and EHR MAARI encounters.
Used logistic regression adjusted for patient age, study site, and month of illness.
Included laboratory-confirmed influenza-positive vs influenza-negative patients from October 2024 to April 2025.
evidence_signal: VE was 36% (95% CI 26–44) in prospective enrollment and 38% (95% CI 36–39) in EHR data, with overlapping confidence intervals for most age groups.
watch_item: Adults aged 65 years and older showed a notable discrepancy between methods, so subgroup estimates may not be interchangeable.
paper_title: Comparison of Influenza Vaccine Effectiveness Estimates Using Test-Negative Prospective Enrollment and Electronic Health Record Data, United States, 2024--2025
